### kernel-red-2 · Answer

Event: `87f20457d8f275f717cee4e3bc483608` · 2026-10-14T20:09:47Z

> Ruling (kernel-red-2, condition 5): option (i), carry rv32's wake_witnesses bound to commit 4's re-measurement. Not a regression.
> 
> Rule served: `wake_witnesses` is a vigour floor, not a rule clause. The clause (scheduling.md 'Preemption points': the answering entry deschedules no runner whose slice has not ended for its own reason) is judged on every wake; at 904354363 all 123 rv32 wakes pass it. The floor guards only against a vacuous pass: enough wakes answered where a preemption could have happened that `wake-preempts` is caught. At 17 call witnesses the negative has 17 chances to fail at its first wrong wake (one suffices); 17 > the stop (10) and > the twin's 5.
> 
> Checked: g4rr-wnph-{1,2,3}.out deterministic 17/34/72; twin rv32 PASS with mid-slice judged at 5; B58's 40-43 on main; toml lines 8-18 already record that under icount the armed hart's interrupt comes after the other hart's call (K31, scheduling.md:1418). Same kind of shift: a cheaper slice end answers more wakes at a slice's end (34) before the spinner's call. Timing-only, held on the twin: (5) satisfied.
> 
> Binding on commit 4: (1) five runs a width alone (not under -j12); rv32's floor set from them with stated margin, never below 10; toml comment and scheduling.md:97-100 give the new ranges and the reason (the slice ends move QEMU's turns, not the rule); (2) re-run `wake-preempts` on rv32 under icount at commit 4 and quote the failing wake, so the floor is shown non-vacuous there, not only on the twin; (3) the twin's wake_mid_slice=5 stays the judge of mid-slice, unmoved; (4) commit 3's report lists rv32 sched-wake-no-preempt-harts as red by this ruling, no toml edit in commit 3; K33 merges only whole, with the gate green. (ii) and (iii) refused: a bound set now is set twice; the construction is B58's and sound.
